questions.learningObjective: Solve a quantitative photoelectric effect problem by applying the governing physical principle.
questions.stem: At 440 nm a photocell of work function 1.50 eV is illuminated. What stopping potential halts the photoelectrons?

options.misconception: Uses the photon energy instead of the electron kinetic energy
Adds the work function to the kinetic energy a second time
Reports the work function as the stopping voltage

questions.explanation: The stopping potential satisfies e times Vs = Kmax = hc/lambda minus work function = 1.32 eV, so Vs = 1.32 volts for a single electron. Using the photon energy, adding the work function, or quoting the work function all ignore that only the excess photon energy becomes electron kinetic energy.
questions.hint: Set e times the stopping voltage equal to the photoelectron kinetic energy.
